Under the UK GDPR there's a legal obligation to respond (correct the data, issue a 3 month extension notice, or refuse with an explanation why) within 1 month, and I said this multiple times, especially when the deadline was fast approaching and then passed, but they didn't even acknowledge it. Many months have passed now and still nothing has been done. A couple of times I asked them to explain why they hadn't made the corrections, and again they just ignored it. Some time before my data rectification request, I had made a formal complaint about a completely unrelated matter, and they are now inexplicably trying to treat these as the same matter. Basically, the complaint response kept being delayed, and when they sent an extension notice, it said "we are working through the separate pieces of correspondence you've sent". The issue though is that the extension notice they sent is only valid for the complaint. This is because the UK GDPR states that the maximum extension time for data rectification requests is an extra 2 months (3 months total) and that this must be issued within 1 month of the original request, when in this situation, no extension notice was provided within anywhere near 1 month, and over 3 months have passed now anyway, so this new extension notice is well outside the legal timeframe for data rectification requests and is only valid for formal complaints, which means that no valid extension notice (or even any meaningful update whatsoever) has ever been given for the data rectification request. They've never attempted to justify or explain themselves. They've never said anything like "sorry, we acknowledge this obligation, but unfortunately we're too short-staffed to uphold it", nor have they ever said "actually, you're factually incorrect, the UK GDPR doesn't mean we're obliged to do this", they're just silently failing to comply with their data protection obligations, even when challenged.
